ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-09-5 (similarity 0.75).
  [R-09-5] Traffic spike and rate limiting - Mitigation (similarity 0.75): Tighten limits on the heaviest caller, raise the ceiling on automatic scaling, and turn away non-essential traffic first. Block abusive sources at the edge. If a client is retrying aggressively, contact whoever owns that client and ask them to back off.
  [R-09-7] Traffic spike and rate limiting - Escalation (similarity 0.70): Call the platform team to raise capacity limits quickly. Tell the business owner about any planned event that nobody mentioned, so capacity can be planned ahead next time. Ask them whether any other region has spare room to take some of the load.
  [R-09-3] Traffic spike and rate limiting - How to confirm (similarity 0.70): Compare the incoming volume with a normal day at this time. If it is several times higher and the machines are busy, this is demand and not a fault. Check whether the automatic scaling has already used up its allowance, and whether one caller accounts for most of the load.

Previous hypotheses:
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: Logs show clear evidence of a traffic spike with partner-api sending 3501rps against a 1000rps limit, triggering load shedding, queue depth warnings, and max autoscaler replicas. (evidence: M-042, L-0277, L-0280, L-0283)
- downstream_timeout: High request durations and 500/502 errors along with upstream 503 responses indicate potential downstream dependency timeout or failure under heavy load. (evidence: L-0287, L-0300, L-0306)
